title: Knowledge check: JSX in Vue

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “JSX in Vue”?
options: Assume every advanced API is stable and behaves identically in every runtime.
Choose an advanced rendering API for a concrete requirement and verify its lifecycle, memory trade-offs, and runtime/version support.
Every view needs Teleport and KeepAlive together.
questions.answer_key: Choose an advanced rendering API for a concrete requirement and verify its lifecycle, memory trade-offs, and runtime/version support.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses JSX in Vue directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.answer_key: Choose an advanced rendering API for a concrete requirement and verify its lifecycle, memory trade-offs, and runtime/version support.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “JSX in Vue” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
